World model: The board still shows only the original colors (G, N, b, Y) plus the pink line (`p`) at the bottom. After scrolling right many times (total of 14 RIGHT actions) no new colors have appeared; the set of object colors remains unchanged. The most recent MOUSE click on the pink line changed the board but was classified as `no_impact` (HUD‑only), confirming that the pink line is part of the HUD band, not a gameplay trigger.  
Goal model: The level’s solution must involve a hidden gameplay element that appears after scrolling further right (or possibly left), but scrolling right up to 14 steps has not revealed any new object colors. The HUD line can be ignored.  
Open questions: – How far must we scroll to expose the hidden element? – Could the hidden element be revealed by scrolling left (perhaps we overscrolled right past it)?  
Plan: Try scrolling LEFT a few steps to see if we have passed the hidden region. We'll scroll LEFT up to 5 times, checking after each move whether any new color (other than G, N, b, Y, p) appears. If a new color appears, we will then investigate that object (e.g., click it).

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
prev_colors = {n['color'] for n in current_frame.segmentation['nodes']}
new_found=False
for i in range(5):
    action(['LEFT'], intent='solve')
    cur_colors = {n['color'] for n in current_frame.segmentation['nodes']}
    new = cur_colors - prev_colors
    if new:
        print('New colors after LEFT', i+1, new)
        new_found=True
        break
    prev_colors = cur_colors
if not new_found:
    print('No new colors after 5 LEFT')
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
